story: Mary Flower, a blues and ragtime fingerstyle guitarist and lap-slide player, moved from Denver to Portland in 2004 and played Pickathon in 2005. She finished in the top three twice at the National Fingerpicking Guitar Championship, the only woman to do so. She was nominated for Blues Music Awards in 2008, 2012 and 2016, and the Cascade Blues Association inducted her into its Hall of Fame in 2018. Folk Alliance Region West named her its Best of the West Artist in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Folk Alliance Region West gave her its Best of the West Artist Award in 2025.

story: The Be Good Tanyas, the Vancouver trio of Frazey Ford, Samantha Parton and Trish Klein, played Pickathon in 2005, after Blue Horse, out in 2000 in Canada and 2001 in the U.S., and Chinatown in 2003. Exclaim called Blue Horse spooky, drowsy gothic folk. Hello Love followed in 2006, the band went on hiatus in 2007, and a Ford song, "In Spite of All the Damage," was used on the Showtime series The L Word. Her solo debut, Obadiah, followed in 2010.
artist_reel_line: A 25th-anniversary vinyl edition of Blue Horse is due in November 2026.

intro: A western-soul band built by two California songwriters.
story: The Hacienda Brothers, a Tucson western-soul band, formed in 2002 when Chris Gaffney and Dave Gonzalez of the Paladins jammed at a friend's 40th birthday party. They played Pickathon in 2005, the year their self-titled debut came out on Koch, produced by Dan Penn, and returned in 2007. What's Wrong With Right came out on Proper in June 2006 and Arizona Motel in 2008. Gaffney died on April 17, 2008, and Gonzalez organized a farewell tour in his honor that summer.
artist_reel_line: Dan Penn produced their self-titled debut and wrote two of its songs.

story: The Shiftless Rounders were a duo of Benny Sidelinger and Phill Saylor Wisor, who met in western Massachusetts and were first based in Vermont. They played Pickathon in 2004 and 2005 and appeared on a live compilation from the festival. Their albums include Ghost in the Radio in 2004 and Warm Clothing Line in 2008, and the band is now defunct.
artist_reel_line: An old-time duo that played in 2004 and 2005; Warm Clothing Line came in 2008.

story: Jug Free America played Pickathon in 2005, the summer the East Bay Express billed its July 14 show at Ashkenaz as its last regular Bay Area appearance before members moved on. The band's final CD is California: 2005.

intro: A banjo player who started Bad Livers in Austin.
story: Danny Barnes, the banjo player who started Bad Livers in Austin in 1990, played Pickathon in 2005, the year Get Myself Together came out on Terminus, after Dirt on the Angel in 2003 and the live Livin' Large in a Little Bitty Room in 2004. He won the Steve Martin Prize for Excellence in Banjo and Bluegrass in 2015 and re-recorded the album that November as Got Myself Together (Ten Years Later) on Eight 30 Records.
artist_reel_line: He won the Steve Martin Prize in 2015 and re-recorded Get Myself Together.
